new.analysis:
The week of Sep 21 – 27 had three planned walk-runs (24, 24 and 27 min) and none were done. Your check-in shows 7.5 hours of sleep, low stress and nothing wrong with your body, so the numbers don't explain the gap. I would rather hear the reason from you than guess.

Next week repeats the missed plan because a short break costs little fitness and you were feeling well. Your last run was Sat Sep 19, nine days before next Monday, and you have already handled 24-minute sessions twice. Total running time comes to 75 min, about 9 min more than your best week so far, and Saturday is the only new step.

The plan holds no faster running, even though the calendar says build. You are still on 2-minute run segments, and what gets you through 5 km without walking is longer unbroken running, not speed. So the build for you is segment length: 3 minutes, then 4 or 5, then longer, with a lighter week before the race.

Your earlier runs felt harder than they needed to. You rated most of them 6 or 7 out of 10 for effort, and a large share of the time with heart rate sat in zone 3. Run segments should feel closer to 4 or 5 out of 10. Going slower now is what makes the longer segments possible later.

The goal is still realistic, but there is little slack. Moving from 2-minute segments to 5 km non-stop in about 6 weeks needs steady weeks with all three runs done. If another week goes missing, we will look again at whether the whole way is realistic for Nov 15 and agree what comes next.

If you feel unwell or anything hurts before a run, skip it and tell me rather than pushing through. Dog walks on the rest days are fine and help recovery, as long as they stay easy.
